title: Attention compression that preserves decisive evidence
objective: Identify a precise task family in which a query-sensitive compression guarantee can preserve retrieval or reasoning outcomes more efficiently than a generic reconstruction objective, and state a falsifiable resource advantage.
deliverables: A primary-literature novelty table distinguishing sparse-plus-low-rank prior art from the proposed contribution
A defined synthetic retrieval task with noise, distractors, rare exceptions, precision, and whole-system resource accounting
One theorem statement with a complete proof attempt and an independent counterexample search
A preregistered smallest falsifying experiment; no experiment results unless actually executed
A synthesis report labeling every claim and recording unresolved disagreement
success_criteria: A nontrivial claim is stated with explicit quantifiers and assumptions, or a documented obstruction explains why it fails
The report distinguishes logits rank, normalized attention rank, value error, and answer correctness
Rare-fact preservation and baseline memory costs are included
A proposed advantage has an observable falsifier and resource-matched baseline
stop_conditions: The assignment or round budget is exhausted
Required source access or mathematical assumptions cannot be established; report the gap
The proposal reduces to existing results without a defensible extension; record and park it
No useful claim survives counterexamples; retain the negative result
